Online and computer-based examinations | products = | revenue = {{down}} {{INRConvert|95.68|c}} (2021) | net_income = {{down}} {{INRConvert|12.26|c}} (2021){{Cite web|title=Aptech Balance Sheet, Aptech Financial Statement & Accounts|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/financials/aptech/balance-sheetVI/A11|access-date=2021-12-18|website=www.moneycontrol.com|language=en}} | assets = {{down}} {{INRConvert|221.31|c}} (2021) | equity = {{down}} {{INRConvert|166.35|c}} (2021) | num_employees = 483 (31 March 2025) | website = {{URL|aptech-worldwide.com}} }} '''Aptech Limited''' is an [[India]]n [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] company that provides [[Vocational education|vocational]] [[training]] and [[education]] services. It was founded in 1986 and is headquartered in [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]].{{cite web | last=Prateek Goyal | first=Avdhesh Kumar | title=Years before NEET row, NTA contracted 2 exam firms with murky record | website=Newslaundry | date=8 July 2024 | url=https://www.newslaundry.com/2024/07/08/years-before-neet-row-nta-contracted-2-exam-firms-with-murky-record | access-date=2 September 2025}} ==History== Aptech Limited was founded in 1986 by Atul Nishar as a [[computer]] [[training]] institute in Mumbai. In 2003, the company was acquired by Kalpathi Suresh, owner of the Chennai-based IT training firm SSI. Two years later, [[Rakesh Jhunjhunwala]] purchased a majority stake and served as chairman until April 2021, when Vijay Aggarwal took over the role. Aptech began conducting recruitment and [[competitive examination]]s in the late 2000s. It reported administering 1.55 million online tests in 2012 and 1.81 million in 2013, including the [[Common Management Admission Test]] across 62 cities in India. ==Controversy== ===Blacklisting Controversy=== Aptech Limited was [[blacklisted]] in May 2019 for three years by the [[Government of Uttar Pradesh|Uttar Pradesh government]] after being found involved in [[fraud]] and irregularities while conducting recruitment exams for government posts. The company's involvement in alleged [[scam]]s in other states including [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[Haryana]], [[Rajasthan]], and [[Assam]] has been documented, with several government recruitment and eligibility exams marred by paper leaks and procedural violations.{{cite web | last=Ali | first=Jehangir | title=Aptech Changed Several Clauses in J&K SI Exam Contract Affidavit; Govt Panel Fails to Highlight Key Edit | website=The Wire | date=27 March 2024 | url=https://thewire.in/law/aptech-jammu-kashmir-sub-inspector-exam | access-date=2 September 2025}} ===Regulatory Penalty=== In 2021, the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] (SEBI) fined Aptech ₹1 crore for violations of [[insider trading]] regulations.{{cite web | last1=Jain | first1=CA Himanshu | last2=Mehra | first2=Ansh | title=Sebi imposes fine of Rs 1 cr on Aptech for violating insider trading norms | website=The Economic Times | date=28 April 2021 | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/sebi-imposes-rs-1-cr-fine-on-aptech-for-violating-insider-trading-norms/articleshow/82296259.cms | access-date=2 September 2025}}{{cite web | title=Sebi fines Jhunjhunwala company Aptech Rs 1 crore | website=The Times of India | date=29 April 2021 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/sebi-fines-jhunjhunwala-co-aptech-rs-1-crore/articleshow/82298994.cms | access-date=2 September 2025}} ===Railway Exam Paper Leak=== In January 2021, Aptech Limited allegated of involvement in the leakage of question papers and answers for the General Departmental Competitive Examination conducted by the [[Railway Recruitment Control Board|Railway Recruitment Centre]] in [[Mumbai]].{{cite web | last=Bharat | first=ETV | title=Railways exam paper leak: CBI registers case against Mumbai-based Aptech Ltd | website=ETV Bharat News | date=9 January 2024 | url=https://www.etvbharat.com/english/bharat/railways-exam-paper-leak-cbi-registers-case-against-mumbai-based-aptech-ltd/na20240109190745859859781 | access-date=2 September 2025}} According to a [[First information report|First Information Report]] filed by the [[Central Bureau of Investigation]], Aptech, which had been appointed as the exam conducting agency, was accused of conspiring to provide candidates with advance access to question papers in exchange for payments ranging between ₹2 lakh and ₹5 lakh.{{cite web | last=Chauhan | first=Ashish | title=Railway Exam Paper Leak: Conspirators Supplied Questions, Answers, and Experts | website=The Times of India | date=24 January 2024 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/railway-exam-paper-leak-conspirators-supplied-questions-answers-and-experts/articleshow/107097546.cms | access-date=2 September 2025}}{{cite web | title=CBI Busts Railway Exam Leak, Raids 12 Places | website=Vibes Of India | date=18 January 2024 | url=https://www.vibesofindia.com/cbi-busts-railway-exam-leak-raids-12-places/ | access-date=2 September 2025}} The investigation suggested that some candidates viewed the papers beforehand at a hotel and received assistance from intermediaries described as exam experts. Reports also indicated that exam results circulated through unofficial [[WhatsApp]] links prior to their formal release.{{cite web | title=Railways exam paper leak: CBI registers case against Mumbai-based Aptech Ltd | website=ThePrint | date=9 January 2024 | url=https://theprint.in/india/railways-exam-paper-leak-cbi-registers-case-against-mumbai-based-aptech-ltd/1916726/ | access-date=2 September 2025}} The CBI initiated searches across multiple locations, naming 15 accused individuals, including railway employees, a CRPF officer, and persons associated with Aptech Limited.{{cite web | title=GDCE Exam: 11 railway employees under CBI scanner in another paper leak scandal involving rupees 4 lakh | website=CNBCTV18 | date=9 August 2024 | url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/education/gdce-exam-11-railway-employees-under-cbi-scanner-in-another-paper-leak-scandal-involving-rupees-4-lakh-19457559.htm | access-date=2 September 2025}}{{cite web | last=Modi | first=Diksha | title=GDCE Exam: 11 Railway Employees Under CBI Scanner in Another Paper Leak Scandal Involving Rs 4 Lakh | website=News18 | date=9 August 2024 | url=https://www.news18.com/education-career/gdce-exam-11-railway-employees-under-cbi-scanner-in-another-paper-leak-scandal-involving-rs-4-lakh-9009826.html | access-date=2 September 2025}}
